variables.variableName: Node number

method.name: Backlit root architecture extraction
method.description: Grayscale backlit RootCam images are segmented with the HADES U-Net-based image-analysis pipeline. Root masks are skeletonized and converted into graph representations. The primary root is reconstructed on the root skeleton using Dijkstra's shortest-path algorithm between the root-shoot junction and the primary-root tip; graph paths and landmarks are then used to derive root lengths and root architectural counts in image-native coordinates. Each image is analyzed independently and temporal continuity is not required for the per-image trait calculation.

variables.variableName: Shoot area (n_pixels_shoot)

method.name: Backlit root architecture extraction
method.description: Grayscale backlit RootCam images are segmented with the HADES U-Net-based image-analysis pipeline. The segmented shoot mask is counted in image pixels to obtain shoot area. variables.variableName: Pixel count in main root ROI

method.name: RootCam ROI mask pixel-count extraction
method.description: Binary ROI masks originate from the backlit RootCam segmentation and are reused by FC_analysis.py. Primary-root and lateral-root masks are transferred directly from segmentation outputs. Root-tip and node ROIs are implementation-defined mask regions used by the fluorescence pipeline. The peri-root ROI is the exclusive region obtained by dilating the full root mask and subtracting the original root mask; root_plus_peri is the corresponding inclusive dilated mask. Pixel count is therefore a channel-independent property of the ROI mask and is not expanded across fluorescence filters or excitation protocols.

variables.variableName: Fluorescence mean in lateral root(s) (filter F448)

method.name: RootCam fluorescence ROI quantification
method.description: A RootCam fluorescence image is acquired using a user-selected FluorCam protocol and emission filter. The raw TAR contains the acquisition protocol, including excitation-channel percentages, filter selection, shutter time and sensitivity. FC_analysis.py extracts the archived .dumm image, horizontally flips it, and applies filter- and FC-unit-specific geometric alignment to the ROI masks generated from the corresponding backlit image. Mean or summed pixel intensity is then calculated within each ROI. ROI pixel counts are represented separately as channel-independent mask variables rather than duplicated by filter.

variables.filterNotes: Common assay mappings used at NPEC: mCherry -> F635; coumarin-related fluorescence -> F483; mTurquoise2 -> F513; GFP -> F513/F520; YFP emission near 596 nm is captured with the HADES F593 filter.

acquisition.lightProfile: Per-acquisition FluorCam protocol from the raw acquisition TAR. The protocol may activate one or multiple excitation channels at user-defined percentages (Act1, Act2, Super, FAR, UV, RBLUE, BLUE, GREEN, AMBER, RED) and also records settings such as Filter, ShutterTime, and Sensitivity.

method.description: A RootCam fluorescence image is acquired using a user-selected FluorCam protocol and emission filter. FC_analysis.py extracts the archived .dumm image, horizontally flips it, and applies filter- and FC-unit-specific geometric alignment to the ROI masks generated from the corresponding backlit image. Mean or summed pixel intensity is then calculated within each ROI. ROI pixel counts are represented separately as channel-independent mask variables rather than duplicated by filter.

method.name: VNIR fluorescence ROI spectrum extraction
method.description: VNIR2 hyperspectral cubes are acquired under 365 nm UV excitation in reflection geometry and corrected using matched dark-reference measurements. Invalid pixels are repaired, spectra are Savitzky-Golay smoothed, and spatial median filtering is applied before horizontal flipping and padding. RootCam masks are transferred to the cube using two-stage registration: a shoot-derived transform against a leaf reference near 670 nm, followed by root refinement against a root-enhanced reference near 410 nm. Final root and exclusive peri-root ROIs are used to export wavelength-resolved mean, sum and standard-deviation spectra.
